name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+40 Philadelphia district makes a Democratic hold near-certain
Rabb outraises independent Mahoney by more than 100-to-1, with $1.6M in outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic win around 96%
No public polling; open seat after Evans' retirement
model.rationale: The district's D+40 partisan lean, paired with an independent opponent who has raised barely $11,000 against Rabb's $1.3 million war chest and $1.6 million in outside support, leaves the Democratic nominee a near-certain winner; markets price the race at roughly 96 percent Democratic.
model.watch: An unexpectedly energetic independent campaign or sharply depressed Democratic turnout could narrow the margin, though the winner is unlikely to change.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
PA-03 is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, anchored in Philadelphia, and Dwight Evans' retirement does little to change its partisan character. Chris Rabb enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.3 million and drawn roughly $1.6 million in outside support, while independent Dennis Mahoney has raised under $11,000 with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls cover the race, but prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances around 96 percent. With only token opposition on the ballot and the district's heavy Democratic lean, Rabb is all but assured of winning, and the main question is the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
